## Nominal is not actual

Plywood sold as 1/4 inch may not measure 6.35 mm. Sheet variation, glue layers, moisture, focus, power, speed, material batch, and machine condition affect the result. Measure the actual sheet with calipers in several places and record the range.

## Kerf changes parts and holes differently

The laser removes a band of material. With a path placed on the intended boundary, an outside part usually finishes smaller while an inside opening usually finishes larger. The exact change must be tested on the local machine and material rather than copied from a universal number.

## Classroom workflow

```text
measure
test
choose fit
modify
cut
evaluate
```

1. Verify a known SVG dimension before cutting.
2. Cut a dimension coupon and compare drawing dimensions with finished dimensions.
3. Cut a tab-and-slot or thickness gauge across a small range.
4. Label results and test with the actual material or mating part.
5. Choose a fit for the function: loose, sliding, snug, or press.
6. Record stock, machine settings, selected dimension, result, and next adjustment.

[Open the calibration library](../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?type=calibration#library) for dimension sheets, kerf tests, fit series, hole tests, and material-thickness tools.
